english.title: Failure to disclose belief / suspicion of financing terrorism
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed to disclose to a constable as soon as was reasonably practicable, your belief or suspicion, and the information upon which it was based, that another person, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME..), had committed an offence under sections 15 to 18 of the Terrorism Act 2000, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..), and that belief or suspicion was based on information which came to your attention in the course of a trade, profession, business or employment
english.legislation: Contrary to section 19(2) and (8) of the Terrorism Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Attorney General is required, section 117 of the Act.
(ii) See section 19(3) and 19(4) for defences.
(iii) See section 19(5) for exemption applying to professional legal advisers.
(iv) For the purposes of this offence a person shall be treated as having committed an offence under one of sections 15 to 18 if he has taken an action or been in possession of a thing, and he would have committed an offence under one of those sections if he had been in the United Kingdom at the time when he took the action or was in possession of the thing, section 19(7).

other.powersofarrest:
Primarily consider: Arrest without warrant - terrorism
Also applicable: Arrest without warrant
other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
